A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VAPO study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM experiments, visual-forgetting analyses, VAPO training results, ablations, and computational measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds claim-quality audits, controlled analyses, additional model comparisons, and new task evaluations.

M1.justification: The default VAPO objective, anchor scoring, late-emphasis weighting, and accuracy gate remain unchanged. v3 adds limited procedural variants: iterative self-generated claims during rollout (B.15), a relaxed-gate curriculum (B.18), and cross-image claim generation (B.23). The expanded filtering description does not establish that the original method was changed.

E1.justification: v3 adds V* and RealWorldQA evaluations for fine-grained perception and spatial reasoning (B.14). More substantially, B.23 introduces explicit multi-image training on a ViRL39K subset and evaluation on BLINK and MuirBench, extending coverage to relationships across images. The original ten benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: v3 Table 24 adds actual comparisons against MM-Eureka, PAPO, and VL-Rethinker, which were cited but not evaluated as comparators in v1. Conversely, v1 Table 15's dedicated comparison against Qwen2.5-VL-3B, InternVL2.5-2B, R1-OneVision-3B, and VLAA-Thinker-3B is removed. The main-table comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The existing main experimental settings are retained, but new studies substantially expand the evaluation design: audits of 500 failures and 250/2000 examples, Qwen3-VL-8B experiments, single-cut recovery at four reasoning depths, difficulty and 300-token length stratification, and a roughly 2500-example multi-image training setting. These are additional protocols, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v3 adds error co-occurrence and claim-quality audits, sensitivity to alternative claim generators, self-supervision tests, single-cut recovery, training/evaluation overlap checks, gate activation and curriculum analyses, anchor-placement comparisons, and reasoning-length analyses (A.3 and B.11-B.22). These test substantial new questions about reliability, mechanisms, and robustness.

E5.justification: No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is added or revised. The new audit percentages and inter-generator differences are descriptive results; the differences written with plus/minus notation in B.12 are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 and the matched supplementary main results and K/beta ablations retain their values. Substantial new results include Qwen3-VL averages of 68.8 for VAPO versus 64.9 for GRPO (Table 16), and multi-image averages of 61.2 versus 58.7 (Table 27), alongside new audit and control findings. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions. v1's dedicated 3B comparison is deleted.

T1.justification: The GRPO and VAPO mathematical definitions and Equations 1-5 are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The new gate discussion is qualitative interpretation, while the single-cut recovery analysis extends an empirical testing procedure.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the dual-nature diagnosis, visual forgetting explanation, VAPO contribution, and benchmark-superiority claims. v3 explicitly emphasizes growing reasoning length, but v1 already attributes deterioration to prolonged reasoning. The added appendix evidence does not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations involving training-data bias and autoregressive objectives, arguments about gate normalization and anchor placement, and interpretations supporting independence from GPT-5 and applicability beyond single-image tasks. It also argues that gains are not merely attributable to longer outputs. However, B.10 retains the single-image-only limitation despite the new multi-image study in B.23.

D1.justification: A.6 newly documents filtering and resampling, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B similarity filtering above 0.95, and claim-diversity constraints. B.9 adds the one-time claim-generation cost of 38 minutes. These are focused reproducibility additions; the main training configuration remains unchanged. The project-page link provided in v1's abstract is omitted from v3.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for selective reasoning, visual instruction tuning, V*, MuirBench, Qwen3 embeddings, and other VLM research, and updates citation placement in related work. The central positioning around visual forgetting and training-based mitigation remains intact. Bibliographic venue updates do not constitute additional research-positioning changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion receive localized edits, and the header changes from preprint to ICLR 2026 publication. The appendix gains B.11-B.23 and loses D.5. Most existing exposition and section ordering remain intact; the expansion primarily reflects added scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial tabular presentation for audits, generation costs, new evaluations, and diagnostic controls (Table 4 and Tables 12-27), removes v1 Table 15, and reflows the appendix. Added appendix prose is displayed in blue. Existing main figures and Tables 1-3 retain their displays, while surviving supplementary tables are renumbered and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical validation by auditing the supervision whose quality v1 identified as a limitation, testing alternative and self-generated claims, probing recovery and gating mechanisms, and demonstrating multi-image applicability. These additions address important uncertainties about reliability and generality, outweighing the loss of dedicated 3B comparisons. Reporting remains imperfect: B.10 still claims exclusively single-image coverage, and B.15's stated average gap disagrees with Table 18's 51.9 versus 52.5. The main benchmark scores themselves are unchanged.
